body:
Slice #258, "The front page shows the last backup", round 1: approved. Every Acceptance criterion holds in the code, each named test exists and exercises the real path (the pure `state` function, `read` against real files, the rendered page through the router, the real binary for the setting, and Playwright against the dev stack and the hosted copy), and the four screenshots show both states correctly at desktop and 390 px.

## Blocking

None.

## Nits

- `Core/assets/core.css:311` (`.backup time`): the relative time is in the mono font, so its word spaces are full cells. "2  days  ago" visibly gaps in `home-backup-stale-*`, and "just now" in mono next to "Last backup" in the UI font reads a little uneven in `home-backup-fine-*`. It follows rule 8 of `design/DESIGN.md` and the slice's Context, so it is not wrong. Whether mono belongs on a relative phrase, as opposed to an exact time, is a matter of taste, and worth deciding once for the whole platform rather than here.
- `Core/src/backup_status.rs:95` (`read`): when the file is missing or unreadable, every front page load writes one `eprintln!` line. That is fine for one user. If the hosted volume is ever left empty, the log gets one line per page view. Not worth changing now, just noting it.
- `Core/src/backup_status.rs:105`: the metadata check and the open are two steps, so a pipe swapped in between them could still be opened. The core only reads a volume that the backup job alone writes, so this is theoretical and does not need a change.

## For the owner

None. I judged each recorded decision, and none of them is one of the three cases that need the owner. Sharing the rounding in `src/relative.rs`, adding `E2E_BACKUP_STATUS_READ` for the restore, showing the failure before staleness, treating a far-future success as unreadable, requiring `last_error`, reading only a regular file, and running the real binary for the settings test are all sound by the implementer's standard. Each is either the stricter option or the one consistent with existing code.

## Replies

None.
